sections.html:
Cicero is a lakeside suburb of Syracuse in the northeastern part of Onondaga County. Oneida Lake lies along its northern edge, the Oneida River marks the border with Oswego County, and Chittenango Creek marks the line with Madison County. The town covers about 48.5 square miles, and Cicero Swamp takes up a large part of the southeast. Interstate 81, U.S. Route 11 and Routes 31 and 298 pass through.

The 2020 census counted 31,435 residents, 0.8 percent fewer than the 31,682 of 2010.

Cicero tax factFigure

Much of the town is wetland, forest and farm land, with new housing developments spreading onto the farmland. Hamlets include Brewerton near the northern line, Bridgeport (partly in Madison County), Cicero Center on Route 31, and shoreline settlements such as Kraus Landing, Forest Beach and Lower South Bay. The Village of North Syracuse lies partly inside the town on its western edge.

Four school districts bill taxes on Cicero parcels. The town's tax receiver processes school taxes for North Syracuse Central Schools, and for the Chittenango, Central Square and East Syracuse-Minoa districts on properties in the town. Buyers will ask which district serves an address, and the school line on the tax bill answers it.

  • Subdivisions include Bay Colony near South Bay, The Crossings, and Lyon's Runne near Oneida Lake.
  • Lakeshore settlements such as Kraus Landing and Valentine's Beach sit on Oneida Lake north of Cicero Center.

The Assessor's office values every parcel in Cicero, handles senior, disability and military exemptions, and tracks sales data and the equalization rate. The town reports a 53 percent level of assessment, so assessed values run well below market value. Judge an assessment against that ratio, not against the price you expect to get.

The next Board of Assessment Review date posted by the town is Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with hearings by appointment only at the Cicero Town Meeting Room, 8236 Brewerton Road, from 12 to 2 p.m. and 6 to 8 p.m. Complaints must be filed by 3:00 p.m. that day on form RP-524, and the town takes them in the Town Hall drop box, by mail or by email.

  • Taxable status date is March 1, and completed exemption applications may be submitted through March 1, 2027.
  • From 2026 the State decides who qualifies for the Basic and Enhanced STAR exemptions, so STAR questions go to the State, not the Assessor.
  • Informal reviews with the Assessor happen before Grievance Day, and the final roll is dated July 1.

Cicero's Receiver of Taxes processes the town and county bill, the North Syracuse village bill and the school bills. The town and county bill is mailed around January 1 and is due without penalty on February 2. School bills are mailed around September 1 and are due without penalty around October 1. Village bills for the part of North Syracuse in town are mailed around June 1 and due July 1.

Partial payments are accepted if nothing delinquent is owed, and the first payment must reach the office by the no-penalty date. Town and county bills can be split into up to four payments, village bills into three, and school bills into three. Mail counts as paid on its postmark date, but a postage meter mark does not count.

Sellers should call the tax office right after a sale. It takes two to three months after a deed is filed with the county for the Assessor's records to show the new owner, and until then the bill goes to the owner on file. Hand the new owner any bill that arrives after closing.

sections.h2: Zoning, permits and certificates of occupancy
sections.html:
The Department of Zoning and Planning issues building permits and enforces the town code from the Town Hall on Brewerton Road. A Certificate of Occupancy is issued once all work under a permit is complete and outside inspection certificates for plumbing and electrical have been received. Anything built without a permit cannot receive a Certificate of Occupancy or a Certificate of Compliance, and the town may issue a stop work order and fines.

Find your zoning on the tax bill or the town zoning map. These are the permit triggers the office lists:

  • Permits are needed to add on, demolish, change occupancy, move doors and windows, repair fire damage or install a fence.
  • Fireplaces, woodstoves and heat-producing devices also need permits.
  • Ordinary repairs, siding, roofing over no more than two layers, and windows or doors of equal size need no permit.
  • A permit lasts 12 months from issue.

Plan review for a new dwelling can run two to six weeks, so settle an unpermitted addition before you list. A direct buyer will often take a house with open permit questions, which a lender-backed buyer may not.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Onondaga County
sections.html:
Deeds for Cicero parcels are recorded by the Onondaga County Clerk. The base fee for a deed is $45.50 plus $5 per page, and transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price. A TP-584 return costs $5, the RP-5217 form costs $125 for improved residential or agricultural property and $250 for improved commercial property or vacant land, and a $10 charge applies to residential deeds.

State law puts the base transfer tax on the seller, at $2 for every $500 of price, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of the deed. Recording is also where a mansion tax of 1 percent attaches to residences at $1 million or more, paid by the buyer.

If you are timing a closing, note that the clerk's office closes every first Tuesday of the month from 10:30 to 11:00 a.m. for a staff meeting.

sections.h2: Selling a Cicero house as is
sections.html:
Cicero sellers can list with an agent, sell on their own, or sell directly to a company like ours. Cash buyers pay little attention to a worn roof or a dated kitchen, and the sale does not depend on a lender's appraisal. You still need a clear title, the tax bills in order and a deed ready to record, and the closing attorney coordinates those pieces.

Before you ask for offers, collect the deed, the latest town and school bills, any permit papers for past work and a payoff statement for each loan. With those in hand the buyer can name a price quickly, and the attorney can order the title search the same week.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cicero, New York?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 31,435 residents, down 0.8 percent from the 31,682 counted in 2010.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day for Cicero property owners?
faqs.a: The next Board of Assessment Review date posted by the town is Tuesday, May 25, 2027. Complaints must be in by 3:00 p.m. that day, and hearings are by appointment.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Cicero property taxes to?
faqs.a: Pay the Cicero Receiver of Taxes at Town Hall, 8236 Brewerton Road, Cicero, NY 13039. The office collects town, county, village and school taxes for parcels in town.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cicero house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: You can sell it, but the town cannot issue a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance for work done without a permit. Call Zoning and Planning to learn what the town would require.

faqs.q: What does the county charge to record a deed in Onondaga County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $45.50 plus $5 per page, with $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential property. Transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price.
